title: metadata-protocol: a commit revert or package-commit rollback can restore a row bound to a read-only base package that the #28905 close now refuses to write
body:
domain:server#5 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQKwKFCp1m6Pb6Q8c1

Source: the contract review of PR #29270 (#28905), record 6577747588, should-fix S1.

#28905 closes the save, publish and rollback doors to a write naming a read-only code package on the five overlay types (`403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, with the pair fix). `revertCommit` and `rollbackToPackageCommit` restore rows through `repo.restoreVersion` (`source: 'protocol.revertCommit'`), outside the save door. So reverting a commit recorded before the close can restore a row bound to the base. The changeset's "Still open" list does not name this path.

Ask: decide and implement one of two. (a) The revert path applies the same close when the restored row would be bound to a read-only base that the pair fix can take, refusing with the same sentence. (b) The path stays open by design, because a commit recorded before the close keeps its revert, as the dogfood control #29090 states. In that case name it in the docs and in the ADR-0087 entry (see the S3 card). Measure first which commits can carry such a row today.

Files: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (the commit doors) and `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`. Serial with the S6 card (same refusal module).
